title: An irreducible scheme with a dense set of rational points is geometrically irreducible
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that an irreducible scheme X over a field k with a dense set of k-rational points is geometrically irreducible (statement lines 1672-1677). By the finite separable characterization it suffices to show that X_{k'} is irreducible for every finite extension k'; so the author takes two irreducible components and proves they coincide. Both project onto X by the behaviour of components under base change, so if they were distinct their intersection would be a proper closed subset whose image under the finite projection is not dense by the standard result that finite morphisms send nowhere dense subsets to nowhere dense subsets (proof lines 1680-1690). Density of the rational points then supplies a k-rational point outside that image; its fibre consists of a single point with residue field k', which must lie in both components, giving the contradiction (proof lines 1691-1696). The claim is H2: a clean contradiction argument whose only inputs are the finite morphism property of the projection and the density hypothesis.
